world.everyday: perfume applied properly, letters written by hand, photographs kept in a box

name: Balletcore
tagline: Discipline that looks like softness
description: Wrap cardigans, leg warmers and satin ribbon - the daily uniform of the studio worn outside it. Delicate on the surface, with real rigour underneath.

world.setting: a studio in the early morning with low sun across a sprung floor
world.architecture: tall windows, a mirrored wall, a barre worn smooth in the usual places
world.interior: almost nothing - a piano in the corner, a bag against the wall
world.technology: a speaker and a timer, both ignored once the music starts
world.clothes: wrap cardigan, leotard, leg warmers pushed down, ribbon tied and tucked
world.music: solo piano, Satie, the same eight bars again
world.colours: powder pink, bone, pale grey, resin
world.everyday: the same exercises daily, sore feet, tiny improvements nobody else sees

name: Soft Pastel
tagline: Blush, hearts and a deliberately gentle world
description: Cloud prints, blush stickers and pastel everything - a self-presentation that chooses sweetness as armour. Internet-native and unembarrassed by it.

world.setting: a bedroom done entirely in pink with fairy lights left on all day
world.architecture: a room in a flat, transformed by everything stuck to its walls
world.interior: cloud-print bedding, plush toys arranged by colour, a heart-shaped mirror
world.technology: a phone in a pastel case, a ring light, a tablet for editing
world.clothes: cropped cardigans, heart clips, blush worn high on the cheek
world.music: bedroom pop, hyperpop turned down, songs with a sigh in them
world.colours: blush, baby blue, lilac, whipped cream
world.everyday: decorating the room again, making things match, keeping the day gentle

name: Dollette
tagline: Prettiness with something wrong underneath
description: Ribbons and lace with a bruise showing - the doll imagery of coquette turned melancholy and a little unnerving. Sweetness used to say something sadder.

world.setting: an attic room with a doll on the shelf that nobody remembers buying
world.architecture: an old house with sloping ceilings and a window that sticks
world.interior: lace gone yellow, a music box, a mirror with the silver flaking
world.technology: none that is working, and one thing that plays when wound
world.clothes: ribbons tied a little too tight, lace, a slip dress, ballet flats scuffed
world.music: a music box, slowed vocals, a piano with a note that sticks
world.colours: faded rose, bone, dust grey, old ribbon blue
world.everyday: long afternoons alone, photographs taken and not shown, keeping things

name: Princesscore
tagline: The fairy tale taken entirely at face value
description: Tulle, tiaras, castles and a ballroom at the end of the story. Unironic fairy-tale fantasy with the volume turned all the way up.

gendered.description: Tulle, tiaras, castles and a ballroom at the end of the story. Unironic fantasy femininity with the volume turned all the way up.

world.setting: a ballroom lit by chandeliers with a staircase made for descending
world.architecture: turrets, arched windows, a palace built to be looked at
world.interior: gilt mirrors, silk drapes, a four-poster with too many pillows
world.technology: nothing - the fantasy does not allow it
world.clothes: tulle skirts, satin gloves, something sparkling in the hair
world.music: waltzes, harp, an orchestra swelling on cue
world.colours: lavender, gold leaf, ivory, pale blue
world.everyday: dressing up for no occasion, believing the story, arranging flowers

name: Royalcore
tagline: Portrait gallery, long corridor, family that owns a county
description: Heirloom jewellery, oil portraits and the weight of inherited rooms. Grander and colder than princesscore, with duty somewhere in the picture.

world.setting: a long gallery hung with ancestors, cold even in June
world.architecture: a stone house with a deer park and a wing nobody uses
world.interior: oil paintings, a library with a ladder, furniture older than the country
world.technology: a bell system, a telephone in the hall, nothing after that
world.clothes: tailoring made to last decades, heirloom jewellery, riding boots
world.music: chamber strings, a church organ, a piano played correctly
world.colours: navy, antique gold, oxblood, parchment
world.everyday: duty before pleasure, the estate before the self, very good manners

name: Angelcore
tagline: Feathers, marble and unbearable light
description: Cherubs, harps and white linen - religious imagery used for its beauty rather than its doctrine. Ethereal, a little mournful, faintly unsettling up close.

world.setting: a marble chapel with light coming down through high clear windows
world.architecture: vaulted ceilings, carved stone, a dome painted with clouds
world.interior: white linen, candles, statuary, dust visible in the light
world.technology: none, and the absence is the point
world.clothes: white linen, gold at the wrist, feathers, bare feet on stone
world.music: choral voices, a harp, reverb that takes four seconds to fade
world.colours: marble white, gold leaf, dove grey, pale gold
world.everyday: quiet, early light, a kind of beauty that is hard to be around

name: Twee
tagline: Small, sincere and slightly out of step
description: Cardigans, bicycles with baskets, indie pop and a fondness for the miniature. A gentle refusal to be cynical, in a world that finds that annoying.

world.setting: a market town on a Saturday with a bicycle leaned against a bakery window
world.architecture: a terraced house with a yellow door and a very small garden
world.interior: a typewriter used sincerely, jam jars, a gallery wall of postcards
world.technology: a film camera, a record player, a kettle that whistles
world.clothes: cardigans buttoned to the top, polka dots, brogues, a beret sometimes
world.music: jangly indie pop, ukulele, harmonies sung slightly flat
world.colours: mustard, sage, cream, faded red
world.everyday: baking for other people, writing notes, taking pleasure in small things

name: Danish Pastel
tagline: Wobbly shapes in sherbet colours
description: Squiggle mirrors, checkerboard rugs and pastel everything arranged with Scandinavian restraint. Cheerful, contemporary and very photographable.

world.setting: a bright flat in spring with the window open and nothing out of place
world.architecture: clean modern rooms, pale floors, one arched doorway
world.interior: a wavy mirror, a checkerboard rug, ceramics in soft colours
world.technology: a small speaker and an espresso machine, both chosen for shape
world.clothes: knitted vests, wide trousers, colours that match the room
world.music: soft electronica, bossa nova, something with a shaker in it
world.colours: sherbet orange, sage, butter yellow, chalk white
world.everyday: arranging, rearranging, coffee at the window, plants that survive

name: Clean Minimal
tagline: Slicked back, gold hoops, nothing extra
description: Glazed skin, a slick bun and jewellery that never changes. An aesthetic of effortlessness that takes a great deal of effort and does not admit it.

world.setting: a bathroom in morning light with everything decanted into matching bottles
world.architecture: a new-build flat with good windows and no mouldings
world.interior: linen, ceramics, one plant, nothing on the surfaces
world.technology: a phone, a facial device, an espresso machine in brushed steel
world.clothes: a white shirt, straight trousers, gold hoops worn every single day
world.music: neo-soul, quiet house, a playlist called something like Focus
world.colours: oat, cream, warm beige, gold
world.everyday: the routine done in order, the same meal, everything put back

name: Cluttercore
tagline: Every surface earns its keep
description: Shelves stacked three deep, walls covered corner to corner, and comfort found in abundance rather than order. The direct answer to minimalism.

world.setting: a front room where every shelf is full and the table has a story on it
world.architecture: an old flat with alcoves, picture rails and radiators that clank
world.interior: books doubled up, postcards to the ceiling, three rugs overlapping
world.technology: a record player, a radio, a laptop lost somewhere under paper
world.clothes: layered, patterned, nothing that matches on purpose
world.music: whatever record was nearest, playing a little too loud
world.colours: amber, oxblood, moss, faded everything
world.everyday: finding things, keeping things, telling people where things came from

name: Kawaii
tagline: Cuteness as a complete worldview
description: Round shapes, mascot characters and pastel everything - a Japanese sensibility that treats charm as worth designing for, right down to the signage on a building site.

world.setting: a shopping street where every shop sign has a face on it
world.architecture: bright shopfronts stacked up a narrow street, all competing
world.interior: shelves of character goods, everything sorted by colour and size
world.technology: a phone hung with charms, a photo booth that smooths your face
world.clothes: pastel layers, character bags, hair clips in pairs
world.music: bright pop with a very high chorus, game music, jingles
world.colours: bubblegum pink, butter yellow, mint, white
world.everyday: collecting, gifting, making the small things nicer than they need to be

name: Fairy Kei
tagline: 1980s toy aisle, worn as an outfit
description: Faded pastels and vintage cartoon characters - a Harajuku style built out of the 80s toys and stationery its wearers were born too late for.

world.setting: a second-hand shop in Harajuku with a whole wall of 1980s plastic
world.architecture: a narrow building with the good shop on the third floor
world.interior: pastel toys arranged like a collection, posters faded to pink
world.technology: a cassette player in a clear plastic case, a toy camera
world.clothes: layered pastels, tulle skirts, vintage character sweaters, ankle socks
world.music: city pop, toy keyboard melodies, twee synth pop
world.colours: washed lilac, sherbet pink, mint, cream
world.everyday: hunting for the rare one, building the outfit, meeting friends to be photographed

name: Decora
tagline: More clips than hair to put them in
description: Dozens of hair clips, stacked bracelets and layered colour to the point of overload. A Harajuku style where the rule is simply: add another one.

world.setting: a Harajuku crossing on a Sunday, being photographed by strangers
world.architecture: a dense street of small shops with signage on every floor
world.interior: a bedroom where the accessories are stored like a hardware shop
world.technology: a phone covered in stickers and charms until it barely fits a pocket
world.clothes: layers of colour, clips from fringe to crown, bracelets to the elbow
world.music: hyper-fast pop, chiptune, anything at 180 BPM
world.colours: every one of them, at full saturation
world.everyday: an hour to get ready, meeting the group, adding one more thing

name: Lolita
tagline: Victorian silhouette, rebuilt by rulebook
description: Bell-shaped skirts, petticoats and blouses buttoned to the chin - a Japanese street fashion with strict internal rules and a deep culture of handmaking.

world.setting: a tea room booked for the afternoon with six people in full coordination
world.architecture: a cafe dressed up in Europe as imagined from somewhere else
world.interior: lace, tiered cake stands, a mirror to check the silhouette
world.technology: a sewing machine that matters more than any screen
world.clothes: a bell skirt over petticoats, a blouse, a headdress, everything matched
world.music: baroque strings, music-box arrangements, chamber pop
world.colours: black and white, dusty rose, navy, wine
world.everyday: sewing, planning a coordinate for weeks, meeting for tea in full dress

name: Gyaru
tagline: Tanned, glossy and answering to nobody
description: Bleached hair, dramatic lashes and nails that make typing hard - a Japanese street style built on deliberate excess and open defiance of what is considered proper.

world.setting: Shibuya at night with the crossing lit like daylight
world.architecture: towers of screens and signage, a department store as a landmark
world.interior: a nail salon, a purikura booth, a bedroom mirror ringed with lights
world.technology: a phone decorated past recognition, a curling iron always warm
world.clothes: platforms, short skirts, lashes, nails as a whole art form
world.music: para para, J-pop, eurobeat at speed
world.colours: bleach blonde, bronze, hot pink, gold glitter
world.everyday: two hours getting ready, going out in a group, being looked at and enjoying it

name: Visual Kei
tagline: The band as a total work of art
description: Androgynous costume, sculpted hair and theatrical staging - a Japanese music scene where the visual presentation carries as much weight as the songs.

world.setting: a live house with the front row pressed against the barrier
world.architecture: a basement venue with black walls and a very good lighting rig
world.interior: a dressing room of mirrors, hairspray and costume on rails
world.technology: amplification, smoke, a lighting desk run like an instrument
world.clothes: costume rather than clothing - leather, lace, buckles, sculpted hair
world.music: hard rock with classical flourishes, ballads that go enormous
world.colours: black, blood red, silver, violet
world.everyday: hours in the mirror, rehearsal, becoming somebody else on stage

name: Jirai Kei
tagline: Pink, black, and not okay
description: Frilled black-and-pink outfits paired with an openly fragile emotional register. A Japanese style that refuses to pretend everything is fine.

world.setting: a cafe in Shinjuku late on a weeknight, alone by choice and not
world.architecture: a narrow building with a different world on every floor
world.interior: a small room, plush toys, medicine on the desk, lights kept low
world.technology: a phone held constantly, a live stream nobody is watching
world.clothes: black frills over pink, ribbon chokers, platform shoes, heavy lashes
world.music: vocaloid ballads, bedroom pop sung very quietly
world.colours: black, sugar pink, blood red, white
world.everyday: nights that run long, texts left unread, dressing up to go nowhere

name: Yami Kawaii
tagline: Cute things saying dark things
description: Pastel plush with bandages and syringes - an aesthetic that uses kawaii vocabulary to talk about illness and despair without softening either.

world.setting: a bedroom that is pink and not restful, curtains closed at midday
world.architecture: a small flat with one window and a lot of time in it
world.interior: plush toys with stitched-on frowns, pill motifs, pastel everything
world.technology: a phone, a drawing tablet, an account posting at 4am
world.clothes: pastel layers, bandage prints, a nurse cap worn as a joke that is not one
world.music: vocaloid, bedroom pop, sweet melodies with bleak words
world.colours: sickly pink, lilac, white, a red that reads as a warning
world.everyday: drawing the feeling rather than saying it, posting, being understood by strangers

name: City Pop
tagline: A bubble-era night drive that never ends
description: Neon reflections on wet tarmac, a convertible on an elevated expressway and a bassline that swings. Japan's 1980s boom years as pure atmosphere.

world.setting: an elevated expressway at 2am with the city sliding past in reflections
world.architecture: glass towers, a hotel bar on the top floor, neon down every side street
world.interior: a low-lit apartment with a city view and a very good stereo
world.technology: a cassette deck in the car, a boombox, a phone with a cord
world.clothes: a linen blazer, sunglasses after dark, gold at the wrist
world.music: AOR, funk basslines, a saxophone that arrives exactly on time
world.colours: neon pink, deep blue, chrome, amber streetlight
world.everyday: driving for the sake of it, late dinners, a city that stays awake

name: Japandi
tagline: Two kinds of restraint agreeing with each other
description: Japanese joinery and Scandinavian warmth in one room - low furniture, pale wood, hand-thrown ceramics and a great deal of empty space left alone.

world.setting: a room with one low table, a paper screen, and light moving across the floor
world.architecture: timber framing, sliding screens, a garden treated as part of the room
world.interior: pale wood, linen, one ceramic bowl that took somebody a long time
world.technology: hidden entirely, or genuinely absent
world.clothes: loose linen, wool in winter, everything in three colours
world.music: a single instrument, long silences, rain on the roof
world.colours: raw wood, oatmeal, charcoal, unbleached linen
world.everyday: tidying as a practice, tea made slowly, nothing bought in a hurry

name: Old Money
tagline: Nothing new, nothing logoed, nothing explained
description: Inherited tailoring, a sailing club and shoes resoled rather than replaced. Wealth expressed by how little it announces itself.

world.setting: a house by the water that has been in the family long enough to sag
world.architecture: a shingled house with a porch, a boathouse, nothing renovated recently
world.interior: worn rugs, sailing trophies, furniture inherited rather than chosen
world.technology: a landline in the hall and a car that is fifteen years old on purpose
world.clothes: tweed, navy blazers, tennis whites, loafers worn to the shape of the foot
world.music: a piano in the next room, jazz standards, nothing current
world.colours: navy, racing green, camel, cream
world.everyday: the same club, the same holiday, spending nothing visible

name: Preppy
tagline: Crested blazer, pastel polo, permanent summer
description: Boat shoes, madras checks and an East Coast campus in early autumn. Bright, conformist and confident, with sport somewhere in every outfit.

world.setting: a campus quad in September with games starting on every lawn
world.architecture: red brick halls, white columns, ivy that is genuinely encouraged
world.interior: a dorm room with pennants, a blazer on the door, a crew photo
world.technology: a laptop and nothing else worth mentioning
world.clothes: pastel polos, madras shorts, boat shoes with no socks, a crested blazer
world.music: a cappella groups, classic rock, something upbeat on the lawn
world.colours: navy, kelly green, pink, white
world.everyday: sport in the afternoon, the same friends since fourteen, being cheerful

name: Yuppie
tagline: Braces, a brick phone and an eighties bull market
description: Power suits, a corner office and a restaurant where the phone is answered by name. Ambition worn as a full outfit, with no interest in hiding it.

world.setting: a trading floor at seven in the morning with every line already lit
world.architecture: a glass tower with a marble lobby and a lift that takes an age
world.interior: lacquer, chrome, a drinks cabinet, a view worth the rent
world.technology: a brick phone, a fax, a terminal glowing green
world.clothes: pinstripe, braces, shoulder pads, a watch chosen to be noticed
world.music: synth-heavy pop, saxophone solos, something playing in the wine bar
world.colours: charcoal, oxblood, brass, city grey
world.everyday: early starts, long lunches that count as work, wanting more

name: Corpcore
tagline: The office uniform, taken seriously as style
description: Lanyards, grey carpet tiles, a pencil skirt and fluorescent light - corporate dress reclaimed as an aesthetic, somewhere between sincere and satirical.

world.setting: an open-plan floor at 6pm with three people left and the lights still full
world.architecture: a glass block with a revolving door and a sign nobody reads
world.interior: grey carpet tiles, a monitor arm, a plant maintained under contract
world.technology: a laptop, a lanyard with a card that opens most of the doors
world.clothes: a pencil skirt or flat-front trousers, a plain shirt, sensible shoes
world.music: whatever is in the lobby, ambient and licensed
world.colours: grey, navy, laminate beige, safety green
world.everyday: the same commute, the same desk, a strange fondness for all of it

name: Hypebeast
tagline: Queued for, resold, and worn once
description: Limited drops, loud logos and a shoe collection kept in the boxes. Status measured in scarcity rather than price.

world.setting: a queue outside a shop at six in the morning for something releasing at ten
world.architecture: a concrete-floored store with one rail and very good lighting
world.interior: shoe boxes stacked like a warehouse, a display of the ones never worn
world.technology: three phones for the draw, a bot, an app with alerts on
world.clothes: a hoodie worth more than the coat, box-fresh trainers, visible logos
world.music: trap, drill, whatever is playing in the shop
world.colours: black, white, one flash of a very specific red
world.everyday: tracking drops, knowing the resale price, dressing for other people who know

name: Mob Glamour
tagline: Fur coat, gold hoops, no apologies
description: Big fur, leopard print, heavy gold and a cigarette held like a statement. Glamour that is loud, adult and entirely uninterested in being tasteful.

world.setting: a restaurant back room where the table is always free on a Friday
world.architecture: a brownstone with a gated front and an enormous kitchen
world.interior: gilt mirrors, velvet, a display cabinet of things nobody uses
world.technology: a phone that rings constantly and a television always on
world.clothes: floor-length fur, leopard, gold layered at the neck, a red lip
world.music: Italian-American standards, disco, something with strings
world.colours: black, leopard, gold, wine red
world.everyday: family first, cooking for twenty, knowing exactly what everything costs

name: Tenniscore
tagline: Pleated whites and a very good backhand
description: Club whites, pleated skirts and the green of a well-kept court. Sporting elegance from an era when the game had a dress code.

world.setting: a grass court in June with the lines newly marked and the net just checked
world.architecture: a clubhouse in white weatherboard with a veranda and a scoreboard
world.interior: honours boards, wicker chairs, a bar that serves one kind of drink
world.technology: a press for the racquet and a machine that fires balls
world.clothes: pleated whites, a cable-knit over the shoulders, clean plimsolls
world.music: nothing during play, a radio in the clubhouse afterwards
world.colours: court green, chalk white, cream, a stripe of navy
world.everyday: practice, the club ladder, strawberries treated as a fixture

name: Equestrian
tagline: Leather, tack room, and up before the light
description: Riding boots, a well-oiled saddle and a yard that needs doing whatever the weather. Country elegance underpinned by early mornings and real work.

world.setting: a stable yard at six in the morning with breath showing and nobody talking
world.architecture: brick stables round a yard, a hay barn, a house behind the trees
world.interior: a tack room smelling of leather and saddle soap, rosettes on the wall
world.technology: a quad bike, a hose, a radio in the feed room
world.clothes: tweed, jodhpurs, long boots, a coat that has seen a decade of rain
world.music: almost none - hooves on concrete and the radio in the background
world.colours: saddle tan, tweed brown, hunter green, straw
world.everyday: mucking out before work, riding in all weather, animals before people

name: Liminal Space
tagline: A place built for people, with nobody in it
description: Empty corridors, shut-down malls and swimming pools at four in the morning. Familiar architecture drained of its purpose, which turns out to be quietly frightening.

world.setting: a shopping centre after closing with the lights still on and nobody left
world.architecture: linoleum, suspended ceilings, corridors that turn one more time
world.interior: a waiting area with chairs nobody is sitting in, a vending machine humming
world.technology: fluorescent tubes, a security camera, an escalator running empty
world.clothes: whatever you happened to have on, which is part of the feeling
world.music: room tone, a distant hum, muzak coming from an unseen speaker
world.colours: institutional beige, fluorescent white, carpet teal, exit-sign green
world.everyday: being somewhere you are not supposed to still be, and not leaving yet

name: Traumacore
tagline: Childhood imagery that no longer feels safe
description: Soft pinks and nursery motifs paired with text that undercuts them. An internet aesthetic that uses the language of innocence to describe its loss.

world.setting: a child's bedroom photographed years later with the wallpaper still up
world.architecture: a suburban house that looks completely ordinary from the road
world.interior: faded nursery wallpaper, a toy box, curtains that never got changed
world.technology: a camcorder tape nobody has watched all the way through
world.clothes: clothes from an age you are no longer, worn anyway
world.music: a lullaby slowed down until it stretches, tape hiss underneath
world.colours: nursery pink, washed lilac, cream gone yellow, faded blue
world.everyday: remembering in pieces, saying it sideways, posting at three in the morning

name: Draincore
tagline: Beautifully bleak, and in on the joke
description: Grainy photos, cigarette ash and the fatalism of a very online adolescence. Nihilism made stylish, with an ironic distance that is not entirely convincing.

world.setting: a stairwell at night, phone in hand, no particular reason to go up or down
world.architecture: a tower block, a car park, anywhere with concrete and a strip light
world.interior: a bedroom lit by a monitor, ashtray on the sill, curtains shut
world.technology: a phone that is essentially a life-support system
world.clothes: a black hoodie, whatever was nearest, the same thing as yesterday
world.music: slowed and reverbed, sad rap, something looping for an hour
world.colours: greyscale, sodium orange, screen blue, cigarette white
world.everyday: scrolling, posting the bleak thing, meaning it and not meaning it

name: Doomer
tagline: Long coat, cold city, no particular plan
description: A grey coat, a beanie and a walk through a post-industrial city at night. Resigned rather than despairing, with a certain grim romance about it.

world.setting: a walk along a ring road at 1am with nothing open and nowhere to be
world.architecture: panel blocks, a closed petrol station, a bridge over a dual carriageway
world.interior: a small flat, one lamp, a window with condensation on it
world.technology: headphones and a phone at nine percent
world.clothes: a long grey coat, a black beanie, boots that have done this before
world.music: post-punk, ambient, one album played the whole way through
world.colours: concrete grey, sodium orange, fog white, coat black
world.everyday: walking to think, smoking in the cold, reading more than talking

name: Scenecore
tagline: 2008 rebuilt from screenshots
description: Neon gradients, pixel hearts and glitter text - the scene era reassembled by people who were too young for it, at twice the saturation.

world.setting: a profile page with an autoplaying song and a cursor trail of stars
world.architecture: none - this one lives entirely on a screen
world.interior: a bedroom with LED strips set to every colour at once
world.technology: a laptop, a drawing tablet, six tabs of GIF hosts
world.clothes: neon layers, pixel-print, hair clips, arm warmers
world.music: crunkcore, nightcore, anything pitched up and sped past comfort
world.colours: cyan, hot pink, acid yellow, black
world.everyday: editing the layout, making the GIF, staying up because it is more fun

name: Glitchcore
tagline: The error made into the image
description: Datamosh, chromatic tearing and images pushed until they break. Beauty found in the failure state of digital media.

world.setting: a screen showing something that is no longer decoding properly
world.architecture: buildings rendered wrong, geometry sliding off its own edges
world.interior: a room lit only by a monitor that keeps changing colour
world.technology: the whole aesthetic - the tools and the subject are the same thing
world.clothes: prints that look like a compression error, RGB split at the seams
world.music: breakcore, glitch, a sample cut to pieces and reassembled badly
world.colours: RGB split, magenta, cyan, void black
world.everyday: corrupting the file on purpose, saving the accident, doing it again

name: Seapunk
tagline: Dolphins, chrome and a 1996 screensaver
description: Aqua gradients, 3D dolphins and Greek busts floating in cyberspace - an early-2010s internet aesthetic built from the visual junk of the dial-up era.

world.setting: a beach that only ever existed as a rendered background
world.architecture: chrome columns and a temple floating over water with no horizon
world.interior: a bedroom with an aquarium screensaver treated as decor
world.technology: early 3D software, a CRT, a CD-ROM of clip art
world.clothes: aqua tie-dye, bucket hats, prints of things that swim
world.music: chopped R&B, house with a whale sample, tape-warped synths
world.colours: aqua, chrome silver, sea green, hot pink
world.everyday: making the graphic, posting it, enjoying how cheap it all looks

name: Synthwave
tagline: Driving into a sunset that is also a grid
description: Neon grids, chrome lettering and a coastline at dusk - the 1980s as remembered by films that were never made. Nostalgia for a decade rebuilt from its soundtrack.

world.setting: a coast road at dusk with the sun setting into a grid on the horizon
world.architecture: chrome and glass towers seen from a distance, never entered
world.interior: a car interior lit red by the dashboard, and little else
world.technology: analog synthesisers, a cassette deck, a car with pop-up headlights
world.clothes: a leather jacket, aviators worn late, nothing practical
world.music: arpeggiated synths, gated drums, a solo at the four-minute mark
world.colours: neon magenta, deep purple, sunset orange, grid cyan
world.everyday: driving with no destination, night as the only setting

name: Mallsoft
tagline: Muzak in a shopping centre that closed in 2003
description: The ambient hum of consumer space, slowed and reverbed until it becomes elegiac. Retail as a haunted landscape.

world.setting: a shopping centre on a weekday with the fountain running for nobody
world.architecture: a glass atrium, planters of fake ficus, escalators crossing overhead
world.interior: tiled floors, a food court with every seat empty, a shop unit papered over
world.technology: a PA system playing to an empty concourse, a payphone still installed
world.clothes: nothing specific - you are a shopper, generically
world.music: muzak slowed to half speed, drowned in reverb
world.colours: mall beige, teal accent tile, fountain blue, brass rail
world.everyday: walking the whole loop, buying nothing, staying past closing in your head

name: Vectordelia
tagline: Swooshes, lens flare and the 1999 CD-ROM
description: Vector swirls, gradient meshes and a lens flare on everything - the graphic design language of turn-of-the-millennium software packaging.

world.setting: the box art of a program you installed once and never opened
world.architecture: an office rendered in 3D with impossibly clean glass
world.interior: a desk with a translucent computer and a mousemat with a swirl on it
world.technology: the aesthetic is entirely about it - beige towers and shiny software
world.clothes: nobody is wearing anything; this aesthetic is pure graphic design
world.music: a start-up chime, corporate ambient, a demo track in MIDI
world.colours: sky blue, cyan, lens-flare white, chrome
world.everyday: installing things, exploring the interface, believing the future is soon

name: Baroque
tagline: Overwhelm as a deliberate strategy
description: Gilded altarpieces, ceilings that open onto painted sky and light used like a weapon. Drama and devotion at a scale meant to leave you speechless.

world.setting: a church at midday with one shaft of light falling exactly where it should
world.architecture: twisted columns, broken pediments, a dome painted to look infinite
world.interior: gilt everywhere, marble in four colours, a ceiling that refuses to stop
world.technology: none - the engineering is the building itself
world.clothes: heavy silk, deep folds, lace at the cuff, everything catching light
world.music: a pipe organ at full stop, strings, a choir in a very live room
world.colours: gold leaf, deep crimson, marble white, shadow black
world.everyday: spectacle treated as a moral good, nothing done by half

name: Victorian
tagline: Every surface covered, every feeling contained
description: Horsehair furniture, patterned wallpaper, mourning jewellery and a parlour arranged by rules nobody wrote down. Industry, propriety and clutter in equal measure.

world.setting: a parlour with the curtains half closed and a clock that is never wound down
world.architecture: brick terraces, bay windows, chimneys in rows down the street
world.interior: patterned wallpaper, heavy furniture, a stuffed bird under a glass dome
world.technology: gas lamps, a mantel clock, a machine that does one thing beautifully
world.clothes: buttoned to the throat, jet beads, a watch chain, gloves indoors
world.music: a parlour piano, hymns, a music box in the hall
world.colours: bottle green, oxblood, mahogany, tarnished brass
world.everyday: calling cards, letters answered the same day, propriety above comfort

name: Regency
tagline: Empire waist, wit, and a long walk to the folly
description: Muslin gowns, assembly rooms and pale neoclassical rooms. Restraint on the surface, with an entire social economy running underneath it.

world.setting: a country house in spring with a walk laid out to a folly on the hill
world.architecture: pale stone, symmetrical windows, a portico and a sweeping drive
world.interior: pale walls, plasterwork, a pianoforte, a writing desk by the window
world.technology: a carriage, a good pen, nothing else required
world.clothes: high-waisted muslin, tailcoats, gloves, a bonnet for outdoors
world.music: a pianoforte in the evening, country dances in the assembly rooms
world.colours: duck-egg, pale stone, straw, soft rose
world.everyday: correspondence, calls paid, long walks, everything said indirectly

name: Neoclassicism
tagline: Reason, rendered in white marble
description: Columns, porticos and plaster casts of Greek originals. The Enlightenment insisting that clarity and proportion are moral qualities as much as visual ones.

world.setting: a museum gallery of white casts with light from clerestory windows
world.architecture: porticos, pediments, columns spaced by a rule you can feel
world.interior: pale walls, a marble floor, statues on plinths at measured intervals
world.technology: none on show - the geometry does the work
world.clothes: simple draped forms, clean lines, nothing that distracts
world.music: a string quartet, formal, structured, resolving where it should
world.colours: marble white, stone grey, pale ochre, olive
world.everyday: study, measurement, the belief that beauty follows from proportion

name: Bauhaus
tagline: Form follows function, and looks good doing it
description: Primary colours, tubular steel and type set without decoration. A school that tried to rebuild everyday objects from first principles, and largely succeeded.

world.setting: a workshop with north light, a bench, and a prototype that nearly works
world.architecture: white render, ribbon windows, a glass stairwell you can see through
world.interior: tubular steel chairs, a plain table, a grid on everything
world.technology: machine tools used honestly, nothing disguised as something else
world.clothes: a boiler suit, round glasses, clothes designed like everything else
world.music: a piano played percussively, early electronic experiments
world.colours: red, blue, yellow, with black and white holding them apart
world.everyday: making the thing, testing it, removing whatever was not needed

name: De Stijl
tagline: The world reduced to lines and three colours
description: Black grids, white fields and rectangles of primary colour. An art movement convinced that stripping everything back far enough reveals a universal harmony.

world.setting: a room where the walls, floor and furniture are all part of one composition
world.architecture: planes that slide past each other, primary colour on a structural edge
world.interior: a chair that is clearly a diagram, a grid of light through a window
world.technology: nothing visible - the idea is the machine
world.clothes: plain blocks of colour, sharp edges, no pattern anywhere
world.music: boogie-woogie piano, rhythmic and gridded
world.colours: red, yellow, blue, black, white, and nothing else
world.everyday: arranging until it balances, removing whatever breaks the rule

name: Impressionism
tagline: Light caught before it moves on
description: Broken brushwork, gardens at midday and a river with the sun on it. An aesthetic of fleeting perception, painted quickly because the light will not wait.

world.setting: a garden at eleven in the morning with the light coming through leaves
world.architecture: a house half hidden by planting, a bridge over a lily pond
world.interior: tall windows, pale rooms, a canvas propped where the light is best
world.technology: paint in tubes, which is the whole reason this could happen outdoors
world.clothes: loose summer cotton, a straw hat, a coat left on the grass
world.music: solo piano, unresolved chords, something by Debussy
world.colours: green on green, lilac shadow, sunlit yellow, water blue
world.everyday: working outdoors, chasing the light, finishing before it changes

name: Surrealism
tagline: Dream logic, painted with a steady hand
description: Impossible objects rendered precisely, deserts with furniture in them and images that feel meaningful without explaining why. The unconscious treated as a place you can visit.

world.setting: a plain that goes on too far, with one piece of furniture in the middle
world.architecture: a doorway standing on its own, a building with the inside on the outside
world.interior: a room where the scale is wrong and nobody mentions it
world.technology: objects that look like machines but do nothing explicable
world.clothes: a bowler hat, a formal coat, something obscuring the face
world.music: a waltz heard through a wall, a voice reciting a list
world.colours: sky blue, desert ochre, deep shadow, bone
world.everyday: writing down the dream at once, trusting the image over the explanation

name: Pop Art
tagline: The supermarket shelf, framed and hung
description: Ben-Day dots, screenprinted repetition and advertising imagery taken seriously. High art shrugging and pointing at a soup tin.

world.setting: a studio that runs like a small factory, with prints drying in rows
world.architecture: a loft with big windows and a freight lift
world.interior: screens, squeegees, stacked canvases of the same image in four colours
world.technology: a screenprinting bed, a camera, a photocopier used hard
world.clothes: a striped top, sunglasses indoors, white jeans with ink on them
world.music: 1960s pop groups, the radio, something with a hook and no depth
world.colours: primary red, yellow, cyan, newsprint black
world.everyday: repeating the image, making more of them, refusing to explain

name: Memphis Design
tagline: Squiggles, terrazzo and rules broken on purpose
description: Clashing colour, geometric confetti and furniture that argues with itself. A deliberate revolt against good taste, and enormous fun about it.

world.setting: a showroom where nothing matches and everything is placed exactly
world.architecture: a white box with coloured columns that hold nothing up
world.interior: laminate in three patterns, a bookcase shaped like a face
world.technology: a radio shaped like a toy, a telephone in bright plastic
world.clothes: blocks of clashing colour, asymmetric cuts, big earrings
world.music: synth-pop with a marimba in it, bright and slightly silly
world.colours: hot pink, cyan, acid yellow, terrazzo speckle
world.everyday: choosing the louder option, laughing at good taste, meaning it anyway

name: Streamline Moderne
tagline: Everything shaped as though it were moving
description: Rounded corners, horizontal speed lines and chrome on a building that will never travel anywhere. The 1930s applying aerodynamics to toasters and cinemas alike.

world.setting: a station concourse with curved walls and a clock built into the plan
world.architecture: white render, rounded corners, horizontal banding, glass block
world.interior: chrome handrails, curved banquettes, indirect light in a cove
world.technology: a radio in bakelite, a train shaped like a bullet, a chrome toaster
world.clothes: tailoring with a long line, a belted coat, everything smooth
world.music: big band, a dance orchestra, something recorded in a ballroom
world.colours: cream, marine blue, chrome, soft grey
world.everyday: travelling well, admiring the machine, believing in the near future

name: Witchcore
tagline: Herbs drying, cat asleep, something simmering
description: Grimoires, jars of dried herbs and a cottage kitchen used for more than cooking. Domestic, practical magic with dirt under its fingernails.

world.setting: a kitchen at dusk with bunches of herbs drying above the range
world.architecture: a low cottage with thick walls and a chimney that draws badly
world.interior: jars labelled by hand, a heavy book, candles burnt to different heights
world.technology: a pestle and mortar, a kettle, nothing that needs a plug
world.clothes: long skirts, an apron with pockets, boots caked from the garden
world.music: a kettle, rain, folk songs sung while doing something else
world.colours: moss, bark brown, beeswax, dried lavender
world.everyday: gathering, drying, brewing, keeping the year by what is in season

name: Strega
tagline: Draped black, Italian folk magic, sharp edges
description: Layered black linen, silver amulets and the severe end of witchcraft - closer to a mountain village than a cottage garden. Elegant, austere and a little forbidding.

world.setting: a stone village on a hillside where the mist comes down by four
world.architecture: stone houses stacked up a slope, narrow steps, shuttered windows
world.interior: bare walls, a single table, herbs and iron hanging by the door
world.technology: none, and it is not an absence anyone notices
world.clothes: layers of black linen, a shawl, silver worn against the skin
world.music: a single voice, unaccompanied, in a language half forgotten
world.colours: black, slate, bone, oxidised silver
world.everyday: walking alone, knowing the plants, being consulted and slightly feared

name: Vulture Culture
tagline: Bones cleaned, catalogued and kept with care
description: Skulls, pinned insects and articulated skeletons - a naturalist's fascination with death that is meticulous rather than morbid. Respect expressed through study.

world.setting: a workroom with specimen drawers and a skull mid-way through cleaning
world.architecture: an outbuilding with good ventilation and a very large sink
world.interior: glass cases, labels in careful handwriting, bones sorted by species
world.technology: dermestid beetles, callipers, a macro lens, peroxide
world.clothes: an apron, gloves, practical clothes you do not mind ruining
world.music: a podcast or the radio, because the work takes hours
world.colours: bone white, tannin brown, specimen-label cream, deep shadow
world.everyday: finding, cleaning, labelling, knowing exactly what each one is

name: Dark Fantasy
tagline: The old stories, with the teeth left in
description: Black forests, cursed kingdoms and heroes who lose things. Fantasy with the moral cost restored - grand, grim and genuinely dangerous.

world.setting: a forest road at dusk where the trees have been listening for a while
world.architecture: a fortress on a crag, a chapel with the roof fallen in
world.interior: a hall lit by fire, banners rotting on the walls, a long table
world.technology: iron, fire, and whatever the smith can manage
world.clothes: layered wool and leather, mail, a cloak that has kept out real weather
world.music: low drums, a bowed string, a horn from further off than expected
world.colours: pitch, moss, rust, tarnished steel
world.everyday: travelling armed, trusting nobody quickly, paying for every victory

name: Granola
tagline: Sourdough, hiking boots and a compost heap that works
description: Wholefoods, hand-knitted layers and a life arranged around walking, growing and making. Practical environmentalism worn every day.

world.setting: a kitchen on a Saturday with dough proving and boots by the door
world.architecture: a small house with a big garden and a shed doing several jobs
world.interior: open shelves of jars, a wood burner, plants on every sill
world.technology: a bread oven, a bicycle, solar panels that paid for themselves
world.clothes: hand-knitted wool, walking trousers, boots resoled twice
world.music: folk, acoustic, the radio while cooking
world.colours: oat, forest green, clay, linen
world.everyday: walking rather than driving, growing some of it, fixing before replacing

name: Afrofuturism
tagline: A future built on an older map
description: Space travel, ancestral pattern and technology imagined outside the usual lineage. A speculative tradition that treats the future as something to be claimed rather than inherited.

world.setting: a city that grew from a different history, with a spaceport in the old quarter
world.architecture: brass and stone domes, geometry drawn from textile rather than temple
world.interior: patterned walls, a shrine and a control panel in the same room
world.technology: advanced and unapologetically ornamented, never grey
world.clothes: printed cloth cut into architectural shapes, gold at the wrists
world.music: cosmic jazz, polyrhythm, synthesisers over hand drums
world.colours: deep violet, gold, malachite, star black
world.everyday: the ancestors consulted about the future, science as a cultural act

name: Afropunk
tagline: Black, loud, and refusing the given categories
description: Sculptural hair, clashing print and punk's refusal reclaimed. A festival, a scene and an insistence on being exactly as much as you are.

world.setting: a festival field in summer where every single person has made an effort
world.architecture: a stage in a park, a city block closed off for the weekend
world.interior: a studio wall of fabric samples and half-finished headpieces
world.technology: a sewing machine, a camera, a sound system
world.clothes: print on print, sculptural hair, metal, nothing bought as a set
world.music: punk, funk, rock and hip-hop refusing to stay in separate rooms
world.colours: black, magenta, gold, jade
world.everyday: making the outfit yourself, showing up as yourself, taking up room

name: Sinofuturism
tagline: Megacity at scale, lit in neon and jade
description: Vertical cities, LED calligraphy and manufacturing at a scale that stops being comprehensible. The future arriving faster than anyone planned for.

world.setting: a street at night under forty floors of signage, all of it moving
world.architecture: towers repeated to the horizon, walkways stacked four deep
world.interior: a small flat very high up, with a window that does not open
world.technology: everything, everywhere, mostly made about a mile away
world.clothes: technical fabrics, a phone as the key to the entire city
world.music: hard electronic, a pop song leaking from a shop, engines below
world.colours: jade green, neon red, concrete grey, LED white
world.everyday: speed, density, everything ordered to the door within the hour

name: Guochao
tagline: Chinese heritage, redrawn for right now
description: Classical motifs on streetwear, calligraphy on a sneaker and dynasty colour palettes used confidently in modern design. Tradition treated as contemporary material.

world.setting: a design district where a tea house and a sneaker shop share a courtyard
world.architecture: a restored courtyard house with glass inserted very carefully
world.interior: lacquer red, a screen, a modern lamp beside an antique table
world.technology: contemporary and everywhere, styled to sit with the old things
world.clothes: streetwear cut with classical collars, embroidery on technical fabric
world.music: guzheng samples over trap drums, pop with traditional instruments
world.colours: cinnabar red, jade, ink black, imperial gold
world.everyday: pride without apology, the old motifs used like any other design tool

name: Wuxia
tagline: Swordsmen, misted peaks and a code worth dying for
description: Flowing robes, bamboo forests and martial artists who move like weather. Chinese heroic fiction where honour is the real plot.

world.setting: a mountain path above the cloud line with an inn somewhere below
world.architecture: a temple on a ridge, timber halls, a courtyard swept every morning
world.interior: a sparse room, a sword on a stand, a scroll and a low table
world.technology: a blade, made properly, and nothing else needed
world.clothes: layered robes that move, a sash, hair bound simply
world.music: guqin, a bamboo flute, long silences between phrases
world.colours: ink black, jade, bamboo green, unbleached silk
world.everyday: training before dawn, travelling light, keeping your word absolutely

name: Gulf Futurism
tagline: A skyline built overnight on top of the desert
description: Air-conditioned malls, glass towers and highways across sand. Extreme modernity arriving at once, with everything older still visible at the edges.

world.setting: a six-lane road at noon with a tower going up on either side
world.architecture: glass towers with no shade, a mall the size of a district
world.interior: marble, cold air, a fountain indoors and daylight kept out
world.technology: the newest of everything, installed before it was needed
world.clothes: immaculate white or black, sunglasses, nothing wrinkled
world.music: lobby ambient, khaleeji pop from a passing car
world.colours: sand, mirrored glass, white marble, sky blue
world.everyday: moving between cooled spaces, the desert visible and never entered

name: Sovietwave
tagline: A future that was promised and quietly cancelled
description: Panel blocks, cosmonauts and synthesiser melodies drenched in longing. Nostalgia for an optimism that belonged to a country that no longer exists.

world.setting: a courtyard between panel blocks in February, snow going grey
world.architecture: identical concrete blocks, a playground of painted steel
world.interior: a small flat with a rug on the wall and a very warm kitchen
world.technology: a radio, a rocket on a stamp, machines built to last and to be repaired
world.clothes: a heavy coat, a fur hat, sturdy boots, nothing showy
world.music: warm analogue synths, a melody that sounds like remembering
world.colours: concrete grey, snow white, faded red, brown linoleum
world.everyday: tea in the kitchen, the same neighbours for thirty years, a future postponed

name: Ostalgie
tagline: Fondness for a country that was abolished
description: East German brand packaging, a Trabant and patterned wallpaper from a state factory. Affection for the ordinary textures of a vanished everyday life.

world.setting: a kiosk on a corner selling the same six things it always has
world.architecture: prefabricated blocks, a cultural centre with a mosaic on the side
world.interior: patterned wallpaper, a wall unit, a television with a doily on top
world.technology: a car you maintain yourself, a radio, a camera with a plastic lens
world.clothes: nylon jackets, practical shoes, a tracksuit worn as normal clothing
world.music: schlager, state radio pop, a synthesiser on a budget
world.colours: mustard, brown, orange, off-white
world.everyday: queueing without complaint, fixing things, knowing everyone on the stair

name: Tropicália
tagline: Brazil with everything turned up and mixed together
description: Clashing print, sunlight, samba filtered through psychedelic rock, and a cheerful refusal to separate high culture from low. Joy used as a political act.

world.setting: a city street in summer where music is coming from three directions
world.architecture: modernist concrete gone green at the edges, tiled façades, shutters
world.interior: bright walls, plants indoors, a record player and not much furniture
world.technology: an electric guitar plugged into whatever is available
world.clothes: tropical print, bright colour, sandals, nothing formal
world.music: samba with fuzz guitar, orchestras colliding with street percussion
world.colours: palm green, mango, cobalt, hot orange
world.everyday: music everywhere, eating outside, treating cheerfulness seriously

name: Brazilcore
tagline: Football shirts, beach heat and green-and-yellow everything
description: Jersey as daywear, açaí, flip-flops and the specific energy of a country where the beach is public life. Casual, communal and loud.

world.setting: a beach on a Sunday with a match happening on the sand and music nearby
world.architecture: apartment blocks facing the water, a kiosk on the promenade
world.interior: a flat with the windows open, a hammock, a fan doing its best
world.technology: a phone, a speaker, a fridge full of something cold
world.clothes: a football shirt, shorts, flip-flops, sunglasses
world.music: funk carioca, samba, pagode from a passing car
world.colours: green, yellow, sea blue, sand
world.everyday: the beach as a living room, food shared, nobody eating alone

name: Hygge
tagline: Candles lit at four because it is already dark
description: Wool blankets, candlelight and the Danish practice of making winter bearable by being deliberately comfortable in company. Cosiness treated as a discipline.

world.setting: a living room in November with the lamps low and rain on the window
world.architecture: a plain apartment with good windows and thick walls
world.interior: wool throws, candles on every surface, pale wood, one good chair
world.technology: kept out of sight, apart from a speaker playing something quiet
world.clothes: thick socks, a knitted jumper, nothing you could not fall asleep in
world.music: soft folk, piano, a record chosen for warmth rather than interest
world.colours: cream, oatmeal, warm grey, candle amber
world.everyday: coffee with friends indoors, early darkness accepted rather than fought

name: Coastal Linen
tagline: Linen, a good kitchen and no one to impress
description: White linen, a garden by the sea and an enormous kitchen used properly. Unhurried comfort with taste and money quietly behind it.

world.setting: a kitchen with the doors open to a garden that runs down toward the water
world.architecture: a shingled house with a porch, weathered grey by the salt air
world.interior: white linen, scrubbed wood, hydrangeas in a jug, cookbooks used hard
world.technology: a radio in the kitchen, a very good oven, nothing else on show
world.clothes: linen shirts, straw hat, flat sandals, a cardigan for the evening
world.music: jazz standards while cooking, the radio, mostly the sea
world.colours: chalk white, sea grey, sand, faded blue
world.everyday: cooking for whoever turns up, gardening, long unhurried afternoons

name: Grandmillennial
tagline: Chintz, scallops and needlepoint, on purpose
description: Floral wallpaper, skirted tables and porcelain, adopted by people forty years too young for it. Traditional decoration reclaimed with full knowledge of how it reads.

world.setting: a sitting room with a skirted table, a lamp on it, and needlepoint cushions
world.architecture: an older flat or house with mouldings that were never stripped out
world.interior: chintz, blue-and-white china on a shelf, a scalloped lampshade
world.technology: hidden inside something wooden wherever possible
world.clothes: printed dresses, cardigans, a brooch worn without irony
world.music: something on the radio, a piano, nothing challenging
world.colours: rose, cornflower, cream, soft green
world.everyday: hosting properly, using the good china, making things by hand

name: Coffee House
tagline: A long table, a notebook and the third refill
description: Dark wood, steam on the window and hours spent writing in public. The café as a room you borrow for thinking in.

world.setting: a café on a wet afternoon with the windows steamed and no rush to leave
world.architecture: a narrow room with a tiled floor, a counter, and tables too close together
world.interior: dark wood, bentwood chairs, newspapers on a rail, a clock that is slightly off
world.technology: a hissing espresso machine and a laptop somebody is ignoring
world.clothes: a heavy coat over a jumper, a scarf kept on indoors
world.music: a jazz record, low, under the noise of the machine
world.colours: espresso brown, cream, brass, tobacco
world.everyday: reading, writing, watching, making one coffee last two hours

name: Midwest Emo
tagline: Twinkling guitars and a house show in a cornfield town
description: Intricate guitar lines, cracked vocals and photographs of empty streets in small American towns. Earnest, specific and quietly devastating.

world.setting: a porch in a small town in August with nothing happening for miles
world.architecture: clapboard houses on a grid, a water tower, a closed main street
world.interior: a basement with a drum kit, a bedroom with a four-track on the floor
world.technology: a cassette recorder, an old amp, a guitar with new strings rarely
world.clothes: a thrifted jacket, jeans, a shirt from a band with sixty fans
world.music: guitars in odd tunings, a voice that goes slightly out of range
world.colours: faded green, dust, cassette brown, evening blue
world.everyday: driving to the next town for a show, writing about here while still here

name: Dark Cabaret
tagline: Weimar theatre with the lights kept low
description: Accordion, smeared greasepaint and a song that goes somewhere unpleasant in the third verse. Theatrical, sardonic and thoroughly adult.

world.setting: a small theatre where the front row is close enough to be uncomfortable
world.architecture: a cellar venue with a stage barely raised and a red curtain
world.interior: bulb-lit mirrors, feather boas on a hook, a piano with rings on the lid
world.technology: a single spotlight and an accordion that has seen better decades
world.clothes: corsetry, tailcoats, fishnets, greasepaint applied heavily
world.music: accordion, a piano played hard, a voice that sneers and then breaks
world.colours: blood red, black, tarnished gold, powder white
world.everyday: rehearsing, performing, saying the unsayable while people applaud
